Safety and security concerns remain a high priority for all affected populations, with displacement contributing to immediate and heightened exposure to violence, exploitation and other forms of abuse. Serious risks and threats to safety and security. The protection needs in Somalia changed and evolved over time. The current crisis affects individuals of all ages and genders, as well as from diverse social backgrounds, in different ways and scale. The most vulnerable groups include people with physical, sensorial, intellectual and mental disabilities, adolescent girls and boys, pregnant and lactating women and girls, female and child-headed households, unaccompanied and separated children, persons from minority clans, older persons without caregivers, persons missing documentation, persons facing eviction, persons living in areas with armed conflict and violence. Women and adolescent girls from 18 – 50 years old (including those living with disabilities) are subjected to Intimate Partner Violence, rape, sexual exploitation, sexual harassment and abuse. Low reporting of GBV cases persist due to stigmatization, victim blaming, shame and interference by clan and religious leaders, slow access to justice and weak or lack of legal framework for the protection of women and girls from GBV. Persons with disabilities face various physical, attitudinal and institutional barriers to access food, health, shelter and protection on an equal basis with others. Persons with disabilities are estimated to be at least 15% of the population and  the majority are among the poorest part of the population. They also face disability-based discrimination, which is exacerbated in situations of crisis, and when it intersects with other factors, such as poverty, gender or age. To mitigate the above mentioned challenge, SSWC will conduct  meetings and consult with people living with disabilities throughout the project phases.  Transportation plans for people living with disabilities will be made for easy access to our centres and our field monitors will ensure that they target households with people living with disabilities in their daily visits within the target areas. Multi-Sector Integrated Approach to Improve Access to Basic Services and Resilience of the Vulnerable Population to the Recurrent Shocks in North Delta Locality, Kassala Improving food security and livelihoods of vulnerable households affected by conﬂict and natural disaster in Blue Nile, North Darfur and Kassala states The project interventions are intended to lead to increased food security & strengthen community resilience to climate shocks &conflict through enabling sustainable increases in agricultural and livestock productivity & adopting alternative livelihoods which will decrease competition over natural resource. The ultimate beneﬁciaries of the project are mainly the farmers and pastoralist, IDPs, returnees & poor residents in Blue Nile, North Darfur and Kassala states (around 580790 people). Agricultural tools, drought resistant seeds & seedlings, vegetables and horticulture will be provided to increase household food production. Promotion of climate smart & resilient crops & livestock production systems, protection of livestock based livelihoods in pastoral & agro pastoral community through provision of emergency livestock assistance, livestock watering, restocking with goat & poultry; awareness raising on the important of healthy diet in addition to women training on food processing for malnutrition, these inputs will build the capacity of the targeted communities to achieve their own food security & improve their livelihoods by increasing their production & income to better able them to withstand future shocks, droughts & other natural disasters. Solar powered women farms will enable produce quality diversified food items for household consumption and income & will reduce work load compared to currently practiced irrigation methods. Establish women saving & loan groups & support it with clean fuel (LPG cylinders & stoves) to establish revolving funds thus reducing wood collection work load & negative health impacts of indoor pollution. Process of women farms will be supported by nurseries, business management & agro processing trainings, linkage to markets & solar lights for safe gathering and mobile charging. The project will support assets protection and increase the ability of the target communities to decrease post-harvest losses & increase their resilience to shocks through provision of cash for work & cash for assets. The project will facilitate regeneration of ecosystem through a range of activities that aims to increase access to water, pasture and forestry which in the past directly contributed to conﬂict between farmers and pastoralists. Training will be provided on the management of these resources and environmental conservation techniques. The project will support the formation & reinforcement of farmers’ groups & community based associations strengthen their institutional capacity and consolidate their links to government service providers & other actors; to facilitate delivery of other project activities. For example, the training & technical support will be provided through these groups. The Project will apply participatory approaches for prioritizing & planning community needs to ensure that community planning & service delivery is tailored to local needs. More over the project will arrange to raise community awareness on themes other than production of the value chain products, including gender, protection & environment. As with elsewhere in the three targeted states men & women have different and unequal access to agriculture and livestock production inputs and technology (women represent about 49% of the total population yet are responsible for more than 65% of agriculture and livestock livelihood activities); therefore the project will ensure that everyone in the affected community women, girls, boys and men have a voice in the development & implementation of the project & have access to opportunities that the project gives. Restocking with livelihoods kits, vegetable growing & marketing will enable women and youth to better engage in income generating activities and production process. The project will be run in environment friendly pattern, saving natural resources & increase target population awareness about environment issues through discussion & orientation sessions.

Improved food security through improved immediate access to food to Pastoral and Agro-pastoral Vulnerable Households in Badade District of Lower Juba region of South Central Somalia Provide emergency Life Saving response, restoration of livelihood assets to protect, strengthen existing livelihood structures for both Rural, Urban Poor and IDP populations and host communities of selected districts in Lower Juba, and Bay regions of Somalia Food assistance needs in Somalia are already high with an estimated 3.5 million people in rural livelihood zones, urban areas, and IDP settlements in need of food assistance. In riverine areas, farmers have suffered from multiple flood events during the Gu and Hagaa 2020 seasons, which damaged Deyr 2019/20 off-season crops and Gu 2020 main season crops. As a result, the main Gu harvest in July/August is significantly below average in these areas. While the floods disrupted recessional cultivation activities and inundated crops, the rains are supporting late planted Gu main season crops and Gu off-season crops and alleviated fears that the forecast of a below-average Hagaa season would deplete soil moisture and negatively affect off-season crops. In general, farmers have benefitted from improved access to water for irrigation. Worryingly however, the damage to road infrastructure and market access, have adversely affected terms of trade with higher prices of maize, and significantly lowering the prices for goats and daily labour wage rates by up to 30 and 102 per cent below the five-year average. 
WRRS will seek to offer response to the needs that has affected both the host community and the IDPs who have sought to take refuge in these proposed areas. This will be attained through improvement of HH access to food by provision of unconditional and conditional cash transfers to the beneficiaries of the targeted district of Bay and lower Juba. Besides this those who are pastorals will receive restock of animals offered with the vaccination, and poultry support with major focus of the female headed HH which will be accompanied by capacity building on best farming practices; veterinary care and pest control. The need to offer sustainable access to livelihood assets in hard to reach areas of Lower Juba and Bay will remain crucial and need urgent humanitarian response especially after the flood that has caused a lot of damage to the previously restored livelihood.
WRRS will work closely with all the stakeholders and other actors to ensure that there is harmornize service delivery without overlap.

SOCIAL PROTECTION Expanding Social, Civic and Economic Engagement and Social Cohesion Interventions for Conﬂict-Affected Adolescents and Youth in the Syrian Arab Republic In support of the ERL Sector (Strengthened Communities and Participation), UNICEF, through this project in 2023, will further support its Generation Unlimited initiative and No Lost Generation Agenda by empowering vulnerable adolescents and youth (10-24 years), female and male and those with disabilities, to access social, civic and economic opportunities for skill development and engagement (including participation in social cohesion initiatives) with the objective of contributing to enhancing resilience and social cohesion. UNICEF will build on strategic partnerships, integration and at scale programming focusing on the most vulnerable adolescents to strengthen skills development, employability and meaningful engagement through friendly spaces and mobile teams. The proposed project will support young women and men to have better access to civic, social, and economic opportunities for skill development and engagement and to unleash their potentials and increase their learning, leadership, and employability opportunities. 
UNICEF will promote the active and meaningful participation of young people brought together from different ages, genders, abilities and cultural and educational backgrounds to be agents of positive change in their communities. UNICEF will work in the following three pillars and related interventions: (1) Provide access to services and skills-building for adolescents and youth for enhanced employability. (2) Strengthen social, civic and economic engagement of adolescents and youth and foster volunteerism and social cohesion-building. (3) Support young entrepreneurs to start their own project projects through seed funding. UNICEF will continue strengthening the capacity of local partners including services providers, youth workers and young volunteers to improve the quality of provided services and enhance the evidence generation. UNICEF will support the scalable and sustainable approaches with national partners including integrated centers & platforms.
In this project, UNICEF will give priority to adolescents and youth in the high severity areas such as Dara’a, Rural Damascus, Northern Homs, Southern Hama, East and Northeast of Aleppo, Deir-ez-Zor and Idleb. UNICEF will expand its support to young people in NES, focusing on returnees and displaced people in Raqqa and Hasakah, including those in camps, collective shelters and urban settings. UNICEF will focus on the most deprived areas in rural and urban areas. These will include camps (Hol, Roj, Newroz, Areesha, Mahmoudli) in Al-Hasakeh and Raqqa , the collective shelters in Al-Hasakeh city, and the rural areas in Qamishli, Malikia, Yaroubia, and Raqqa Governorate. Projects engaging young people will be essential needs for their effective integration in their communities. In addition, since 2014, many young people have been staying in camps and collective shelters. They do not enjoy the freedom of movement and face other risks, thus offering them activities that will enhance their skills and allow them to catch up to their peers in terms of skills and non-formal education.  The programme will coordinate with and support other UNICEF programmes to ensure interventions are tailored to the particular needs of young people. The programme will implement activities for young people affected by, or at high risk of, emergencies or the socio-economic situation, to acquire the right skills, become empowered and resilient community members who help their communities to cope with emergencies. Life-skills and citizenship education for these adolescents will equip and empower them to act as both participants and catalysts of change in their community as volunteers and peer influencers.

Durant l’année 2019, le contexte sécuritaire du Centre et Nord Mali ont été marqué par la recrudescence des violences de la population. Ces violences ont occasionné de nombreux déplacés internes vivant dans des conditions précaires. Les differents rapports d’évaluation rapide et conjointe produit par les inter-agence humanitaires ressortent que 03 ménages de sur 04 n’ont pas d’abris. Le problème d'accès en eau potable dans ces sites de déplacés n’a pas été épargné. Cet accès limité à l’eau ainsi que les conditions d’hygiène et d’assainissement précaires favorisent les maladies d’origine hydrique et à potentielle épidémique dans les sites des déplacés où familles d’accueils. Ce qui explique un besoin fort en abri et de EHA.
Pour palier à ces besoins, NRC propose à travers ce projet d’apporter sa contribution afin d’améliorer les conditions des personnes touchées dans un environnement sécurisé avec un accès aux logement et aux infrastructures Wash. 
NRC construira et réhabilitera des points d’eau, forages, puits, et mettra également en place des comités EHA et Abris avec 50% de femmes accompagné d’un mécanisme de suivi. NRC mettra en place les latrines d'urgence accessibles aux handicapés avec des kits de lavage des mains en tenant de l’aspect genre et de protection avec un emplacement visibles et separées entre les femmes et les hommes. Des poupelles pour la gestion des ordures seront mise en place dans les sites. 
Le projet se focalisera sur une reponse avec la formation sur les techniques de construction des maisons/abris suivi d’une distribution de kit abri constitué de matériaux locaux adaptés aux zones. Les différentes couches d’âges de déplacés bénéficieront de cette formation. Pour le cas des déplacés vivant en location dans les zones urbaines, NRC se pensera sur une possibilité d’une assistance de Cash. Ce Cash pouvant contribuer à soulager les charges de loyer des déplacés. Au niveau des sites inappropriés et appropriés, le respect des normes de construction et de sécurité des logements seront prise en compte dans son appui technique nécessaire aux déplacés pendant l’auto construction des maisons. Il veillera au respect de la distance prevue entre abris et infrastructures. Il se convergera sur le renforcement au respect du genre par les communautés à travers des sensibilisations sur l’égalité des sexes. NRC mettra en place plusieurs activités en commençant d’abord par une évaluation de base, des enquêtes CAP permettant d’avoir des informations de référence, les prises de contacts avec les partenaires et les leaders communautaires des déplacés. Cela dans le but de définir les approches à mettre places et les critères de ciblage. NRC ciblera la population extrêmement vulnérables avec un accent sur le genre et les personnes a besoins spécifiques. Ces groupes de personnes représentent un risque de protection plus élévé Lorsqu’elles sont dans une situation de deplacement. NRC s’assurera que son assistance ne nuira pas à la sécurité de ces personnes y compris l’environnement dans lequel ils vivent. 
NRC optera à une méthodologie de sélection des bénéficiaires en tenant compte des orientations des partenaires externes. Les aspects protection et sécuritaire ne seront pas négligés. Ces partenaires, bénéficiaires seront impliqués dans le processus de ciblage. Pour éviter toute exclusion lors du processus de ciblage, une analyse des risques de protection liée à la réponse de NRC sera entreprise. Des mecasnismes des plaintes sera mise en place.
Pour maintenir la collaboration et les efforts entre les acteurs dans le secteur Abri et Wash, NRC participera activement aux réunions de coordination et forums humanitaire au niveau national et régional organiser par OCHA, les 2 Clusters, des instances gouvernementales et niveau des sites des déplacés pour discuter des questions problématiques liées aux déplacés. Il participera à la conception des outils d’évaluation, aux évaluation des besoins, au rapportage, à l’harmonisation des kits.

Area-Based Response: Provision of life-saving Health, Nutrition, WASH, and Protection services for the displaced people affected by crises and fighting in Gezira state Comprehensive humanitarian nutrition services for IDPs, returnees and vulnerable residents  The humanitarian nutritional needs in Sudan are expected to remain at high levels or worsen further in 2023, making Sudan one of the countries in the World with highest estimated acute malnutrition caseload.  While the overall Global acute malnutrition (GAM) remains at 13.6%, the prevalence of GAM varies significantly across the localities with very high situation (GAM above 15% and above as per WHO classification) reported in 64 localities. The proposed nutrition project aim is to improve equitable access to quality life-saving curative and preventive services through the systematic provision of nutrition services in South Kordofan, North Kordofan, Central Darfur, North Darfur, West Darfur, Sennar, Blue Nile and Red Sea states in which 29 localities will be covered. Vulnerable children under-five and PLWs are the main target of the project. Through SC -Nutrition interventions, a total of 362,874 beneficiaries will benefit from the services provided, among them (87,131 boys, 90,680 girls, 184,383 women, 680 men). Save the children will implement lifesaving, preventative interventions, treatment of severe and moderate acute malnutrition among children under five years and Pregnant and Lactating Women (PLWs), referral of SAM children with medical complications and minor rehabilitation to nutrition sites. To reach the estimated targets and planned response scale up, the nutrition sector will deploy integrated response modalities with health sector, WASH, FSL, protection, education at facility and community levels. SC will deliver nutrition services through existing health facilities, mobile and outreach teams and at community such as mother-to mother support groups activities including IDPs and hard to reach areas, use of cash-based interventions to increase access and utilization of nutrition services through FSL will be used for most cases in need. In term of emergency response, rapid response mechanisms for timely delivery of nutrition interventions in the onset emergencies will applied.

Specific nutrition response strategies will include scaling up the minimum preventive and protection lifesaving intervention package for prevention of malnutrition, treatment, and geographical coverage of severe and moderate acute malnutrition among the under-fives, strengthening referrals for children suffering from SAM with medical complication through provision of transportation costs to and from the SC, nutrition system capacity strengthening (capacity and infrastructure) will be done to facilitate provision of quality and people centered life-saving nutrition responses, timely procurement and delivery of core nutrition supplies. Additionally, infant young child feeding (IYCF) and social behavior change, and communications (SBCC) will be strengthened to promote good feeding and access to services. SC will strengthen national and sub national partnership with all stockholders to deliver nutrition services. SC will ensure monthly and quarterly monitoring of the evolving nutrition situation through an early warning and early actions and implementation of SMART surveys in prioritized localities with GAM 20% and above as well as supporting other assessment initiatives such S3M and MICS.
